statement: New-building jobs on lots in the 2015 preliminary 1%-annual-chance floodplain fail to reach a certificate of occupancy within 36 months of their first foundation permit more often than jobs elsewhere in the same borough.

graph_evidence.summary: The graph has no finding on flood rules and construction duration. Its vacant-land findings (PMIDs 23814668, 36716893) concern the consequence of land left vacant. The repo's tidal-flooding claims (further-tidal-flooding-*) concern flooding, not building.

literature.citation: NYC Building Code Appendix G (flood-resistant construction), amended 2013 after Hurricane Sandy
literature.finding: Buildings in the 1% floodplain must elevate or flood-proof to the design flood elevation plus freeboard, adding design review and cost.

literature.citation: NYC DCP, Zoning for Coastal Flood Resiliency (2021)
literature.finding: Text amendment allowing height to be measured from the flood elevation; framed as removing a zoning obstacle to building in the floodplain.

literature.citation: FEMA preliminary FIRM 2015 for NYC (used for building code since 2015)
literature.finding: The 2015 preliminary maps enlarged the 1% floodplain; Red Hook lies wholly within it.

prediction.magnitude: Mantel-Haenszel borough-stratified risk difference, flood minus non-flood, of the 36-month no-CO rate: +0.04 to +0.15.
prediction.support_if: lower 95% bootstrap bound of the stratified risk difference > 0
prediction.refute_if: upper 95% bootstrap bound of the stratified risk difference < 0

plan: Script analyses/stalled/flood_predictor.py, mode 'run', committed with this registration. 3,410 foundation starts in the windows 15 Dec-14 Jun of 2017-2023 (from vesting_cohorts.py); 3,276 match current PLUTO, 401 of them in the 2015 preliminary floodplain (BK 121, BX 19, MN 30, QN 198, SI 33). Outcome stalled_1096 from vesting_exploratory.py (no CO by job number or BBL within 1,096 days). Bootstrap 2,000 draws, seed 20261113, within borough x flood strata. Power check (rule 8): with a rate near 0.38 the standard error is about 0.026, so a true difference of 0.10 gives z_null about 3.9 (D = 15); the test discriminates for differences above about 0.055.
alternatives: Neighbourhood market: floodplain lots in Queens and Brooklyn are in Rockaway, Coney Island, Red Hook and Gowanus, where demand differs (borough stratification only partly removes it)
Project size: large waterfront projects take longer than 36 months whether or not flood rules slow them
The current PLUTO flag describes the lot today; lot changes after the permit can misplace a job
Selection: the flood rules may deter weak projects before foundation, leaving stronger ones (biases toward no difference)
